title: Improvement Candidate Record
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Safe Self-Improvement and Rollback Database (public edition), a database that tests improvements before release and restores the last known-good version when needed, under a recorded gate. Improvement Candidate Record covers the following: describes a proposed improvement, its source experiment, and the gates it must pass. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How it works

A candidate improvement is tested in stages against the fixed suite and the regression suite, and it is promoted only when it passes every gate; if a promoted change later fails its triggers, the recorded rollback procedure restores the last known-good version. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: describes a proposed improvement, its source experiment, and the gates it must pass. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo compares a candidate gate score with the known-good gate score and prints the promotion decision. The demo program prints:

Candidate gate score: 78 points
Known-good gate score: 80 points
Decision: HOLD (rollback target stays pinned)

Use and limits

Staged testing reduces risk but never removes it. A candidate can pass every gate on the fixed tasks and still fail on unseen tasks, which is why rollback triggers stay armed after promotion. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record details

Record fields: candidate_version: candidate v1; known_good_version: known-good v0; gate_result: all gates pass; rollback_trigger: cost budget crossed; task_class: retrieval of existing records.

print('Known-good gate score: ' + str(known_good) + ' points')
print('Decision: ' + decision + ' (rollback target stays pinned)')
